objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (19 November 2026) on RING-IDENT-20261119-001#1 (relays, 3/3, 3/3): when a finite piece of the extended candidate complex with no cycle and no chain finishes while other pieces still hold loose distinctions, its top is not implied and gets one fresh distinction. Prove the count with a relay (a point carrying two endless chains attached at the top) added, starting with the path of five knots and the spider; stop at a proof, or the first relay that is not one such point. Then tally the census's trees by number of chains. Serves G17.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Successful; refereed R1, confirmed): relays proved (a finished piece's top carries one point with two endless chains when another piece is live, and closes otherwise; 218 of 218 small starts agree); a tree start's dimension is the largest number of chains in a piece, a finished piece counting two; on the touch census, 307 of 307 simple trees agree, and growing simple trees are two-dimensional in 266 of 292 (3,753 of 4,055 with double touches, on DOUBLE-IDENT): why two is typical there; the other 61% of two-dimensional growths have cycles of three or four knots, outside the proofs.
stop_rule: Stop at a proof, or the first relay that is not a point with two chains at the top.
title: Relays: the count when a finished piece goes on
